insight.title: The CEO Who Ignored Profits to Save His Company
insight.subtitle: How focusing on a non-financial metric saved a failing giant.
insight.notificationHook: A new CEO banned profit talk

sections.text: In 1987, Alcoa’s new CEO, Paul O’Neill, met anxious Wall Street investors. Instead of discussing revenue, he announced his sole priority was reaching zero workplace injuries.
Terrified investors immediately dumped their stock. But O’Neill stayed firm, forcing managers to redesign dangerous, chaotic factory floors to prevent even minor accidents.
By eliminating safety hazards, Alcoa streamlined its entire manufacturing pipeline. Operations became flawless, waste vanished, and annual net income soon increased by 500 percent.
The best way to improve a number is to ignore it.
